Thought: To determine how a heterozygous single nucleotide substitution appears on a chromatogram, we need to understand what a chromatogram would look like when there is a heterozygous variant present. In chromatograms, DNA sequencing data is represented by peaks for each nucleotide. In the case of a heterozygous single nucleotide substitution, both alleles are present in the sample, leading to two different nucleotides at the same position. This will typically manifest as two peaks of approximately equal height at the same position since both alleles contribute equally to the signal.
